chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

O Muhammad ibn Muslim! The sins of the believer, when he repents from them, are forgiven for him. So let the believer do [good deeds] for what he resumes after repentance and forgiveness. By Allah, they are not [for anyone] except for the people of faith.

I said, 'And if he returns [to sin] after repentance and seeking forgiveness from the sins, and returns [again] to repentance?' He said, 'O Muhammad ibn Muslim! Do you see that the believing servant regrets his sin, seeks forgiveness from it, and repents, then Allah does not accept his repentance?'

I said, 'Indeed, he does that repeatedly, sinning then repenting and seeking forgiveness of Allah?' He said, 'Every time the believer returns with seeking forgiveness and repentance, Allah returns upon him with forgiveness. And indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. He accepts repentance and pardons the evil deeds. So beware that you do not cause the believers to despair of the mercy of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: Does a believer's repeated sins prevent Allah from accepting their repentance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) emphasizes that repentance (tawbah) is a continuous, dynamic process for the believer, where repeated sins are met with repeated divine forgiveness as long as sincere remorse persists. He warns against 'qanoot' (despairing of Allah's mercy), a subtle spiritual trap that can halt the cycle of repentance, thereby linking the acceptance of forgiveness directly to the believer's hope in God's infinite mercy. This narrative underscores the Shia theological balance between accountability and the boundless nature of Allah's rahmah, encouraging persistent spiritual renewal rather than fear of finality.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘O Muhammad Bin Muslim!

The sins of the Momin when he repents from these, are Forgiven for him, so let the Momin do (good deeds) to what he can resume after the repentance and the Forgiveness. But, by Allahazwj! It is not for anyone except for the people of Emān’.

I said, ‘Supposing if he repeats after the repentance and the Forgiveness from the sins, and repeats in the repentance?’ So heasws said: ‘O Muhammad Bin Muslim! Do you see that Momin servant regretting upon his sin and seeking Forgiveness from it and repenting, then Allahazwj does not Accept his repentance?’

I said, ‘Supposing he does that repeatedly, sinning then repenting and seeking Forgiveness of Allahazwj?’ So heasws said: ‘Every time the Momin repeats with the seeking of the Forgiveness and the repentance, Allahazwj Repeats upon him with the Forgiveness, and that Allahazwj is Most-Forgiving, the Merciful. Heazwj Accepts the repentance and Forgives the evil deeds. So the Momineen should beware from despairing from the Mercy of Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Once abu Ja’far (a.s.) said, ‘O Muhammad ibn Muslim, if believing people repent for their sins they will be forgiven. Believing people must resume their good deeds after repentance and forgiveness. By Allah, this is only for the believers.’

I then asked, ‘What if he goes back to sin after repenting and asking for forgiveness and repents again?’ The Imam said, ‘O Muhammad ibn Muslim, do you think a believing servant (of Allah) regrets his sins, asks forgiveness and repents but Allah does not accept his repentance?’
I said, ‘He, however, has done it many times. He sins, repents and asks forgiveness (from Allah).’

The Imam said, ‘Whenever a believing servant (of Allah) returns back for repentance and pleas for forgiveness, Allah returns to him with forgiveness; Allah is forgiving and merciful. He accepts repentance and effaces the evil deeds. You must never cause a believer to lose hope in the favor and mercy of Allah.’”
